groups.label: State, society and outlooks
groups.note: Outlook advocacy never substitutes for the exact governing-party gate. These are optional political actions, not prerequisites for the ruling party programme.

groups.label: Le Duan — revolution and reunification
groups.note: Historical starting programme. First Secretary in 1970; General Secretary title only from the 1976 congress. Military pressure and negotiation can coexist.

groups.label: Truong Chinh — doctrine or reassessment
groups.note: Historical party chief July–December 1986. Early accession or a prolonged tenure is alternate history. A short historical tenure can complete the opening reforms; the full programme represents a longer mandate.

groups.label: Nguyen Van Linh — Doi Moi
groups.note: Historical party chief from December 1986. Economic renovation preserves communist rule unless the player separately negotiates a political opening.

groups.label: Vo Van Kiet — practical government
groups.note: The existing mod leader pool can select Kiet, although he was never historical party chief. This full personal-leader programme is explicitly alternate history; historical cabinet influence is represented in common pilot decisions, not by falsely renaming his office.

groups.label: Fatherland Front — independent socialism
groups.note: Uses existing 1970 Front slot 19. Historically a communist-led umbrella, not an independent governing competitor. Its autonomous neutral-socialist rule is an explicit alternative settlement.

groups.label: Democratic Party — constitutional government
groups.note: PROPOSED 1970-specific slot 2 mapping replacing the later-era default name. The real Democratic Party was a Front ally; independent government requires a negotiated opening or rupture through existing politics. Nghiem Xuan Yem, Democratic Party Secretary-General 1958–1988, is the proposed era-specific leader. He was an agricultural engineer and Front ally; an independent liberal government is counterfactual.

groups.label: Socialist Party — a pluralist left
groups.note: PROPOSED 1970-specific slot 3 mapping. The northern Socialist Party is a real patriotic-intelligentsia Front ally; this pluralist governing role is alternate history, not the southern Hoa Hao Democratic Socialist Party. Nguyen Xien, Socialist Party Secretary-General 1956–1988, is the proposed era-specific leader; Hoang Minh Giam is a secondary cabinet/leadership alternative. Their independent pluralist programme is counterfactual.

groups.label: VNQDD — nationalist republicanism
groups.note: Native VNQDD slot 0. A northern return needs amnesty/repatriation or a major political rupture. Western is the MD outlook family, not a claim that all nationalists accept foreign tutelage.

groups.label: Military government — security or transition
groups.note: Existing armed-forces slot 22, explicitly alternate history. Dai Viet civilian nationalists can advise the administration, but are not falsely mapped onto a new fascist party. Civilian-return choices use the real political system.

groups.label: Reconstruction, energy and industry
groups.note: Physical capital persists across governments. State-targeted projects require owned/controlled territory, native capacity and treasury. No 2000-era grants or future technology.

groups.label: Food, cooperatives and living standards
groups.note: Rural insecurity already matters in 1970. The 1971 flood or a new blockade is a contingent later crisis, never an accomplished starting fact.

groups.label: The People’s Army and civil defence
groups.note: No starting armies/equipment are changed. This is doctrine, organisation, repair and funded infrastructure; specialised forces still depend on actual equipment and the existing research system.

groups.label: War, Paris and national integration
groups.note: Multiplayer diplomacy requires recipient agreement. Paris is not automatic reunification. A victory route needs actual ownership; integration never silently annexes or cores another player’s land.

groups.label: Two patrons, regional security and the world
groups.note: Soviet, Chinese and neutral routes share realistic dependence costs. Other countries answer offers. Neither treaty signing, aid, sanctions removal nor Cambodian/Chinese wars happen by unilateral focus reward.
